descriptionChirho: The proper noun Samuel (Hebrew שְׁמוּאֵל), referring primarily to the prophet, priest, and last judge of Israel, son of Elkanah and Hannah, who anointed both Saul and David as kings. All 140 occurrences denote this same individual (with a minor secondary referent in 1 Chr 7:2 for a Levitical genealogy). The two-cluster split is purely syntactic: 136 occurrences as bare or conjunctive forms vs. 4 with the preposition לְ ('to Samuel'). Multilingual evidence is unanimous: eng 'Shemuel / Samuel / to Shemuel,' spa 'Samuel / a Samuel,' hin शमूएल / शमूएल से, arb صَمُوئِيل / لِـ صَمُوئِيل, kor 사무엘이 / 사무엘에게, swa Samweli / kwa Samweli.
